claims.text: Not a different build: both editions use the same container images and identical install process
Enterprise obtained via license key from Kasten or cloud marketplaces
General install prerequisites must be met
GKE node pool must have Compute Engine set to Read Write
Cluster accessible via kubectl
Service Account with access to underlying storage; GCP SA plus auto-created Kubernetes SA
Dedicated namespace e.g. kasten-io, pre-created with kubectl or created in Marketplace wizard
Default GKE install needs volumesnapshotclass annotated k10.kasten.io/is-snapshot-class
Marketplace can create K10 and reporting service accounts (may need IAM admin) or use pre-created ones
Strongly recommended to install in a dedicated non-default namespace

A.notes: Does not say Free is functionally the same but limited in support and scale.

claims.text: Free uses same container images and identical install process as Enterprise
Free is functionally the same but limited in support and scale
Kasten requires a k10-cluster-passphrase secret before install
Kubernetes Service Account auto-created during helm or Marketplace install
kubectl must have proper access to the cluster
A GKE cluster is required for installation on Google Cloud
A separate GCP Service Account with appropriate permissions is required
kasten-io namespace can be pre-created or created during the wizard [10]
Kasten can be deployed using the GCP Marketplace on GKE
Enterprise (PAYGO) Red Hat Marketplace license warning requires RHM registration and operator

B.notes: Presents the optional passphrase secret as a requirement; the source calls the separate SA 'preferred', not required; [10] is only a screenshot caption; RHM warning is OpenShift-specific and irrelevant; misses Compute Engine Read Write.

claims.text: EM uses OAuth with Microsoft Graph API and an access token from Microsoft identity platform; needs a registered application
Register an app and obtain client ID, tenant ID and client secret
Grant Mail.Send application permission plus delegated email, offline_access, openid, User.Read; Mail.Send.Shared for shared mailboxes [3]
Log in with Portal Administrator role, Configuration > Notifications
Server Settings tab, select Microsoft 365 from Mail server list
Enter Application client ID, Tenant ID, Client secret; Save
Click Authorize now and allow EM to access the M365 account
EM also supports Google account or SMTP with basic auth

A.notes: [3] is the Veeam Backup for Microsoft Azure appliance notification page, not Enterprise Manager, so the delegated-permissions list is not supported for EM; misses redirect URI/account type and registering-account requirements.

claims.text: EM offers Microsoft 365 as a mail server option in the Notifications section
EM sends via the Microsoft Graph API [2]
EM uses OAuth 2.0 authentication
Needs client ID, tenant ID and client secret of a Microsoft Entra application
Application must have Microsoft Graph Mail.Send permission
MABS v4 UR2+ can send through Microsoft 365 using OAuth 2.0 client credentials [10]
MABS requires STARTTLS for such notifications
SMTP AUTH must be enabled for mailboxes or tenant

B.notes: [2] resolves to the step list without the Graph API sentence; [10] is the client-secret step, not the MABS v4 UR2 statement; no step-by-step EM procedure or app-registration details; padded with irrelevant MABS content.
